bugs.summary: Firefox fails to select email addresses in BT email

comments.author: c.r.allen@btinternet.com
comments.creator: c.r.allen@btinternet.com
comments.raw_text:
User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:147.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/147.0

Steps to reproduce:

* Write an email (doesn't even need to be forward)
* Begin typing in the "To:" field, autocomplete options appear
* Select an autocomplete option (mouse or cursor)

Actual results:

* The autocomplete prefix is used as the email address rather than the selected email, obviously, as this is not a valid email address it appears with a red border.

Expected results:

* The selected email address is used as the "To:" address.

This makes BT email basically unusable from Firefox.

comments.author: mozilla@keithcirkel.co.uk
comments.creator: mozilla@keithcirkel.co.uk
comments.raw_text:
Bob and I took a look at this, this morning. Unfortunately it's a little tricky to debug, but some overall comments:

1. We can consistently reproduce. 
2. It seems to be a racey timing issue; using a debugger to break on the mouse listener code point "fixes" the issue. I suspect this might be to do with event timing or a mixture of async/sync code.
3. Observing the minified code: it seems to be pre-hooks React code, so using classes with `render()` and `this.setState`. We observed several setters on the class object (`this.state.shouldFocusInput` & `this.state.optionIndex` or similar), these setters interleaved with `this.setState` could be triggering the racey behaviour - as `this.setState` is asynchronous. 

Unfortunately the use of React makes this a really tricky debug due to React's synthetic event system which adds a lot of entry points and can be very difficult to follow (especially in minified code). We tried using React Devtools but their deployment either A) predates React Devtools or B) has the various symbols/hooks compiled out in the production build.
